edits.before: Data shows the Ashley Phosphate Road and I-26 intersection in North Charleston averages a crash every 3 days — making it the most dangerous intersection in South Carolina. Here's why, and what your rights are if you're injured there.
edits.after: A Post and Courier analysis of 2011–2015 collision data recorded 629 crashes at the Ashley Phosphate Road and I-26 intersection in North Charleston — about one every three days, the most of any intersection in the tri-county area and second in the state. Here's why, and what your rights are if you're injured there.
edits.note: post_excerpt called it the most dangerous intersection in South Carolina; the page's own body says it ranked SECOND statewide. The excerpt renders as the Article `description` in schema, so the false claim was being published as structured data after the body, FAQ and takeaways had all been corrected.

edits.before: Ashley Phosphate Road and I-26 is the most dangerous intersection in South Carolina, averaging a crash every 3 days. Learn about truck accident risks, common crash types, and your legal rights.
edits.after: Ashley Phosphate Road and I-26 is among the most crash-prone intersections in South Carolina, averaging a crash every three days in a Post and Courier analysis of 2011–2015 data. Learn about truck accident risks, common crash types, and your legal rights.
